2) Confirm backup storage location and retention controls (can be scoped to EU only).
3) Detail logging: what metadata is stored centrally vs customer-managed, retention windows, and options for redacting PII from logs.

I'll loop in Aditya from Product (technical lead on region routing) and Laura on the compliance side for the follow-ups below.

Marissa —

Appreciate the recap. A few clarifying questions from security/infra:

1) Backups: Are snapshots and backups guaranteed to remain within the EU (no copies to US regions for redundancy)? We need this for regulatory reasons.
2) Failover: If eu-west-1 has an outage, what is Redwood's recommended cross-region failover model? Can we opt out of automatic cross-region failover and configure an on-demand failover that requires our approval?
3) Logging / PII: Our policy requires that any request/response PII not be stored in plain text in centralized logs. Can you confirm what is captured in Redwood's control plane logs, and whether we can redact or ship logs to our SIEM only (no storage in Redwood's central logs)?

If you can answer those upfront, we can determine whether to have our infra lead on Monday's call.

Thanks —
John Patel
Head of Cloud Security, Acme Bank
john.patel@acmebank.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-14T09:12:00Z
Subject: Re: Data residency follow-up and next steps (region pinning)

John —

Thanks — answered inline below and adding Aditya + Laura to provide the detailed technical/compliance confirmation.

1) Backups:
- By default, snapshots for Dedicated/Private deployments are stored in the pinned region (eu-west-1) and we offer a policy toggle to keep backups region-local.
- We can provide a contractual commitment in the Private/Dedicated SOW that backups will not be copied out of the EU unless Acme explicitly authorizes cross-region replication for DR.

2) Failover:
- Our recommended model for high-availability is active-active across multiple AZs inside the pinned region. Cross-region failover is optional.
- We support an on-demand failover policy: Redwood can hold automatic cross-region failover disabled and only fail over after a manual approval step from an authorized Acme contact. This is available in Dedicated and Private deployments (we'll document the runbook).

3) Logging / PII:
- Control plane logs include telemetry (request IDs, model/version, latency, token counts) but do not persist full request/response payloads by default. PII-containing fields can be redacted at the ingestion layer.
- We support customer-managed log export (forward to your SIEM/Kinesis/Logstash). When enabled, we can set retention to 0 days in Redwood's central logs and keep archives only in your environment.

Aditya / Laura — could you attach the short diagram and a one-page compliance summary that calls out: backups region policy, failover options (auto vs manual), log retention options, and KMS/HSM key controls for encryption?

Marissa

From: John Patel <john.patel@acmebank.com>

Thanks Marissa — that addresses most points. Couple quick follow-ups:

• Can you confirm whether snapshots used for backups include KV cache contents? If so, can those caches be excluded from backups or encrypted with customer-managed keys?
• For the on-demand failover runbook: is there an SLA for the failover decision window? E.g., Redwood will wait up to X hours for manual approval before initiating predefined actions. We need that clarified for our BCP.

Also — please share the compliance one-pager and architecture diagram prior to Monday so our security lead can review. If possible, please flag any items that would require a contractual addendum.

John

Subject: Re: Data residency follow-up and next steps (region pinning)

John —

Appreciate the precise asks — attaching the two artifacts (diagram + one-pager). Quick answers while you review the attachments:

• KV cache in snapshots: snapshot behavior depends on deployment mode. For Dedicated/Private we can exclude in-memory KV cache from persistent backups; otherwise caches are ephemeral and rehydrated on warm start. For your pilot (Dedicated in EU) we will exclude KV caches from persistent snapshots and can encrypt snapshot artifacts with your customer-managed KMS key.
• Manual failover SLA: default runbook is to await a manual approval for up to 4 hours. After 4 hours we will escalate to the on-call contact list and, if still not approved, follow your pre-agreed fallback policy (could be automatic failover or continued wait) — we will include that as an explicit option in the SOW.

Next steps:
1) Aditya/Laura to confirm no additional items (attachments attached).
2) Can we lock Monday 11/16 10:00 AM CET for the technical deep-dive? Please provide attendee list.
3) If the diagram and one-pager look good, we'll draft the SOW language for backup locality + manual-failover SLA and route through your procurement.

Thanks —
